The Pokémon TCG's 30th Celebration Ultra-Premium Collections have finally arrived, but getting hold of either the Espeon (Day) or Umbreon (Night) edition at a reasonable price has been proving difficult, even with new listings regularly going live across major U.S. trading card retailers.

Released on Nov. 6, these enormous anniversary boxes have become two of the most sought-after Pokémon products of the year — just as much as the 30th Celebration ETB. Along with the many early Pokemon Black Friday deals, we've found several places to buy both versions, with Walmart at the moment offering the lowest prices among top retailers. However, there are some important differences between the available offers and the official restocks.

We've rounded up the retailers worth checking out, the latest prices, and everything you need to know to secure one of these special collections ahead of Black Friday.

These are the main U.S. retailers to bookmark for the Espeon and Umbreon collections, including their current stock situation:.

Amazon: Stock is coming and going directly from the retailer and third-party sellers, so we’ve added a go-to search results page to quickly check for any restocks (we expect more this week).

Best Buy (Day and Night): Official stock is hard to find, but third-party listings are still available for both versions. Set up deal alerts to catch any upcoming allocations.

Target (Day): Currently sold out via official stock and third-party sellers.

TCGplayer (Day and Night): The dedicated trading card marketplace has listings for both the Espeon and Umbreon editions of 30th Celebration’s Ultra-Premium Collection at around or under market price.

Walmart (Day and Night): Both Day and Night editions are available through third-party sellers. Keep an eye out for cheaper listings.

Demand for the 30th Celebration expansion has been exceptionally strong since its September launch, and these Ultra-Premium Collections are arguably the hottest items in the entire anniversary lineup.

In a recent development, unlike smaller Pokemon products such as Booster Bundles and Elite Trainer Boxes, each UPC contains a staggering 30 booster packs, including one exclusive Classic Collection pack with three etched cards celebrating the TCG's history. Add in two highly collectible promo Pokémon cards — Espeon and Umbreon — alongside special Pikachu ex promo cards and all the premium extras (playmat, card sleeves, deck box, etc.), and it’s no wonder that there hasn’t been enough supply to meet the demand.

There are two versions to choose from: the green-and-blue Day edition featuring Espeon ex, and the purple-themed Night collection starring Umbreon ex.

It has been revealed that both contain 29 standard 30th Celebration booster packs and one special Classic Collection pack, alongside a foil Pikachu ex promo card and a matching Espeon ex or Umbreon ex promo. You'll also get a themed playmat, 65 card sleeves, a deck box, a metal Pokémon coin, six damage-counter dice, and a code card for Pokémon TCG Live.

The accessories and promotional artwork vary between editions, but you’re effectively getting the same level of contents with either box.

With both versions in high demand, there are a few ways to make tracking down an Espeon or Umbreon Ultra-Premium Collection a little easier:.

Recent findings suggest that keep checking the major retailers: Walmart, Target, Best Buy, Amazon, and GameStop are all worth revisiting throughout the week — as new stock has been constantly reappearing over the last couple of weeks. According to recent reports, set up stock alerts where available: Retailer notifications and independent stock trackers can help you spot fresh inventory without repeatedly refreshing every product page. Best Buy, for instance, even lets you set deal alerts for specific listings.

It has been revealed that compare prices across different sellers: Third-party sellers can be a useful way to secure either collection when official stock is unavailable. Just remember to compare their offers against current market prices (available on TCGplayer), as some listings are considerably more expensive than others.

Check whether you're getting Day or Night: Some retailers list the two versions separately, while GameStop uses combined listings with randomized selections. Make sure you're ordering the right product if you're specifically after Espeon or Umbreon.

Don't overlook in-store availability: Online stock shifts incredibly fast, but checking nearby Target, Best Buy, and GameStop locations could give you another chance to grab a box — as many don’t check physical stores, simply assuming they’ll be automatically sold out, particularly if additional inventory arrives ahead of Black Friday.

It's certainly possible that more Ultra-Premium Collections could come in stock for Black Friday, though no allocations have been confirmed for either collection.

With Black Friday arriving on Nov. 27, there's still a little over two weeks for retailers to receive more inventory and, as mentioned, there have been fleeting stock drops across the major Pokemon TCG retailers — even if most of them come via third-party sellers. Keep in mind that due to the demand for the 30th Celebration UPCs, sellers have little incentive to discount listings much below market price (around $360 per Ultra-Premium Collection).

For now, it's worth keeping the retailer pages above close at hand, so you can compare prices for any available stock and decide what’s best for your trading card budget.

Tech Report: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on November 16, 2026

💡 Key Takeaways
  • We're almost at the First Quarter Moon, which is when we'll see half of the lunar surface illuminated.
  • 16, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Crescent phase, with 39% of its surface visible.
  • In a recent development, if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Tranquillitatis, Fecunditatis, and Serenitatis.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We're almost at the First Quarter Moon, which is when we'll see half of the lunar surface illuminated. From here, the Moon will continue to grow until we reach the Full Moon again.

As of Monday, Nov. 16, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Crescent phase, with 39% of its surface visible.

In a recent development, if you don't have any visual aids, you can still see the Mares Tranquillitatis, Fecunditatis, and Serenitatis. With binoculars or a telescope, you'll also see the Endymion Crater, Posidonius Crater, and the Mare Nectaris. And for keen Moon gazers with a telescope, you'll get to see all this plus the Apollo 16 and 17 landing spots, as well as the Rima Ariadaeus.

The next Full Moon will take place on November 24.

Sources indicate that the Moon takes approximately 29.5 days to complete one full cycle. As it orbits Earth, the amount of sunlight reflecting off its surface that we can see changes, creating the different phases. This takes us from the Newly introduced Moon to the Full Moon and back again, before the cycle begins once more, according to NASA.

Newly introduced Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye).

Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere).

Recent findings suggest that first Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon.

Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet.

Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible.

It has been revealed that waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere).

Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit.

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The global economy is "on the AI leg," International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva noted Monday, warning that the overdependence on the sector risks the world's financial stability.
  • Georgieva flagged that a "sudden drop in investment confidence and withdrawal from the AI field" could weaken economic growth, speaking with CNBC's JP Ong on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations' summit in the Philippines.
  • In a recent development, "We have a world economy that is standing on one leg on the AI leg.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The global economy is "on the AI leg," International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva noted Monday, warning that the overdependence on the sector risks the world's financial stability.

Georgieva flagged that a "sudden drop in investment confidence and withdrawal from the AI field" could weaken economic growth, speaking with CNBC's JP Ong on the sidelines of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations' summit in the Philippines.

In a recent development, "We have a world economy that is standing on one leg on the AI leg. If this leg wobbles, that can lead to financial stability troubles," Georgieva warned.

In a recent development, circular financing among AI companies — where money invested in an AI tech giant ultimately flows back to the investor through purchase orders — has grown to a little over $1 trillion, two-thirds of it funded by debt, the IMF estimates. "It's not a huge size, but it is a rapid increase," Georgieva said.

Nvidia Corp, which has seen more than $1 trillion wiped out of its market value over the past month, is at the center of these circular financial deals. The fallout from the chipmaker's former CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese spy, has led to a sell-off in global AI-linked stocks and put the spotlight on the company's role as a key financier of the AI infrastructure buildout.

UBS analyst Tim Arcuri estimated in a recent note that an Nvidia financing pullback could easily remove $50 billion or more out of the system, at a time when rising interest rates have already made corporate borrowing more expensive.

Georgieva's warning comes as the AI build-out has been a critical engine of growth for the global economy, propping up trade and investment.

The IMF raised its 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% in October as major economies lean on AI investment to power growth otherwise curtailed by the energy crunch caused by the Iran war.

Sources indicate that the institution estimated that about 40% of the world's workforce will be affected by AI. Capital Economics suggested that as much as 80% of the recent expansion in global exports was concentrated in AI-related goods.

Investors' frenzy for AI reflects expectations running ahead of what the technology has proven to deliver, Georgieva stated. "We tend to rush ahead," as valuations climb, she said, therefore "some corrections" become necessary.

It has been revealed that IMF in October had warned that a short-term disappointment could set off a disorderly correction across asset classes: in its worst case scenario, if AI fails to live up to the market's lofty expectations, U.S. equity prices could fall 20% in 2026 and global output end up 1.1% below its baseline estimate by 2028.

Global equites, including U.S. chipmakers, have been seeing a bruising sell-off over the past few weeks, with investor appetite for the AI trade facing a fresh test this week ahead of earnings from Nvidia and Anthropic's blockbuster listing.

Georgieva on Monday characterized the recent market swings as "orderly," and unlikely to spiral into anything that could undermine the world economy, while urging caution. "We have to be watchful.".

There are two main reasons people still buy standalone cameras despite having an iPhone in their pocket wherever they go. The first is lens quality: iPhones have small plastic lenses compared to the far larger and more sophisticated glass lenses used with dedicated cameras.

In a recent development, the second is sensor size. All other things being equal, a larger sensor will capture more light and provide a higher quality image. Current smartphone sensors are absolutely tiny compared to those used in even mid-range consumer cameras.

In a recent development, we’ve seen two previous reports suggesting that a larger sensor is on the way for future iPhones. One of these suggested that it would be coming in 2027 or 2028, although a later one suggested the latter date was more likely.

The reports were not without a catch, however, suggesting that the larger sensor would only be for the telephoto lens and would have a 200MP resolution. Squeezing more pixels into a given sensor size tends to sacrifice low light capabilities in return for higher resolution. This is less likely to be an problem with a telephoto lens, which is normally used outdoors rather than inside.

What I’d really love to see is a significantly larger sensor for the main camera, with no increase in resolution. This would improve low light performance and overall image quality.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Microsoft has now explained what went wrong, stating that the mistake that led to the failure was actually made all the way back in July without being detected ….

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Last week saw a truly epic outage to Microsoft 365, with a huge number of consumers unable to send and receive emails. The company has now admitted that at the worst point, more than 80% of its servers were unresponsive.

Microsoft has now explained what went wrong, stating that the mistake that led to the failure was actually made all the way back in July without being detected ….

It has been revealed that the firm said at the time that it was a technical concern and not a cyber attack, and that it was working hard to fix the problem, admitting that it was taking longer than expected. Microsoft also denied that it was related to the thousands of layoffs revealed the previous month.

People were understandably unimpressed at the scale of the outage and the time taken to fix it, although meme creators were having fun.

Industry observers note that sorry but you have to be change the name now. Thems the rules pic.twitter.com/5UttZ8nt9f.

It certainly points out that when you base your business on cloud services, you also take the risk that comes with that.

Platform head Charles Lamanna admitted the severity of the problem.

In less than two hours, the previously unknown defect was encountered across our fleet and rendered them unresponsive. At its lowest, more than 80% of servers were unresponsive.

He noted it resulted from a combination of two challenges. The company maintains two independent network gateway systems, one of which failed, meaning that the remaining gateway took the full load. That wouldn’t have been a problem on its own, Microsoft stating that each one has enough capacity to handle all traffic. However, a mistake made back in July led to a cascading failure.

It has been revealed that A latent defect caused servers to become overwhelmed and unresponsive under certain load conditions. This was due to lock contention inside an internal process which caused the machine to become unavailable. This defect was the result of a fix that was prepared specifically for Microsoft 365 networking gateway servers […].

The initial change in behavior first started deployment in July of this year. The upgrade went through safe deployment and saturated globally over several weeks, during which time no issues were observed. For more than three months, the change was deployed worldwide without impact. Our normal load testing did not detect the latent concern because the different traffic and SKU mix used in our test labs. The contention issue is worsened on machines with more cores and newer hardware; whereas our load testing tended to focus on our weaker hardware SKUs with fewer cores.

In other words, the update wasn’t tested under the conditions in which it was most likely to fail.

It has been revealed that while the company claims that the incident is unrelated to laying off staff and replacing them with AI systems, I find myself extremely skeptical. It seems inconceivable that a company of Microsoft’s size could make what appears to be a schoolboy error of this magnitude unless there were insufficient engineers working on the patch. Please share your own thoughts in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia's stock slid 4.12% Monday in the wake of CEO Jensen Huang's resignation, leading a broader chipmaker selloff after the chip giant lost hundreds of billions in market cap last week.

The continued decline since Huang's resignation brought Nvidia's stock to its lowest close since July 1, 2025.

Huang resigned from Nvidia, the manufacturer's board announced on Thursday, after mounting scrutiny following reports that he had a relationship with a woman believed to be a Chinese spy. Huang told employees he had an affair in an email on Nov. 8.

It has been revealed that it was later reported that Huang had romantic relationships with two Nvidia employees. Nvidia did not immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment on Friday.

Recent findings suggest that an online petition calling for Huang's reinstatement as Nvidia CEO has drawn more than 170,000 signatures, as prominent tech executives, including Elon Musk, rallied behind him. A source familiar with the matter told CNBC, however, that Nvidia's board of directors is not considering bringing back Huang.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, U.S. lawmakers are pushing to launch comprehensive investigations into the scandal.

Huang cofounded Nvidia in 1993 and led the firm through its meteoric rise to becoming the world's most valuable company, with its AI chips underpinning the technology's boom.

Nvidia appointed longtime finance chief Colette Kress as interim CEO and said its board would consider both internal and external candidates in its search for a permanent successor.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a "dramatic shakeup" at Nvidia, adding that the board should look outside the organization for its next chief executive.

He also suggested other Nvidia executives should face scrutiny over the chip giant's compliance with U.S. export controls.

— CNBC's Caleigh Keating contributed to this report.

Updated November 2026: I added chargers from Peak Design and Mophie, removed some older devices, and updated links and prices.

Recent findings suggest that packing space is often limited when you travel, so it’s very handy that Anker’s MagGo folds down to a slim, compact form. It can feel a little crowded when fully loaded, but I appreciate the space-saving design when packing it in a bag. While you can find faster options with chargers that support Qi2 25W, they’re not widely available and make little difference if you charge your devices overnight.

Recent findings suggest that this cute, compact charging kit comes in a soft faux-leather bag. ESR’s folding charger delivers 25-watt charging for Qi2 25W-supported phones, fast Apple Watch charging, and an effective cooling fan. The fan is relatively quiet, but I prefer total silence at night, so I was pleased to find a button that turns it off for when you’re trying to sleep.

Recent findings suggest that the plastic construction doesn’t feel premium, but it is lightweight, and the rubber feet do a decent job of preventing it from sliding around. Sources indicate that with a clean white finish, an elegant folding design, and warm ambient light, this Journey charger is a delightful travel companion. Ordinarily, I hate superfluous lights on a charger, but this isn’t a pointless LED; it’s a gentle glow from behind the Apple Watch shelf on the back, with a touch-sensitive power button on the front. It’s nice to have when you wake up in an unfamiliar, pitch-dark hotel room. You can fold it out to stand mode to charge all three Apple gadgets at once, or lay it flat if you just need to charge your iPhone and AirPods.

Recent findings suggest that while this folding charger isn’t quite as compact as Anker’s below, I love that you can use the iPhone charging pad when it’s folded up. The Apple Watch charger can also pop up for Nightstand mode. It’s finished in a soft faux leather and folds flat for easy carrying in the included pouch. If you are really pressed for space, this is the smallest three-in-one charger you can get. Unfolded, you get a magnetic pad to charge your iPhone at up to 15 watts, a middle pad for your AirPods, and an Apple Watch charger on the right. The design is lovely to handle, with a soft-touch finish and a durable silicone strap. I still prefer stand-style chargers because they allow you to angle your iPhone and use StandBy mode, but the MagGo UFO lets you travel as light as possible.

It has been revealed that more stylish and compact than the other options listed here, this two-in-one charger from Peak Design folds flat for easy stowing. Open it to reveal a base with a channel for a USB-C cable and a Qi2 25W charging pad, plus a second swiveling Qi2 25W pad on top. You can charge two phones, or a phone and wireless earbuds. There’s also a USB-C port on the side, so you can plug in a third device, or a watch or ring charger. It comes with a cable, but you’ll need a power adapter (45-watt minimum). I like Peak Design’s 65W Dual Slim Charger ($65), but you don’t have to spend that much.

In a recent development, this genius petite gadget is perfect for folks who love to travel light. It’s an Apple Watch charger with a handy carabiner you can clip to your key ring or bag strap. Rotate the magnetic pad, and a USB-C jack pops out. Just to be clear, this is not a power bank—you must plug it into your MacBook, a USB-C port on a wall adapter, or even your iPhone to charge your Apple Watch. It doesn’t get more portable than this.

UAG 3-in-1 Travel and Desktop Charger.

Recent findings suggest that UAG SRGE 3-in-1 Travel and Desktop Charger for $100: This charger was close to earning a top spot until I saw the price (regularly $165). It’s a very smart charging kit that folds flat and comes in a snazzy zip-up bag with a 4-foot braided USB-C cable and a 25-watt power adapter, including plugs for the US, UK, and Europe. You can prop your iPhone at different angles on the MagSafe stand, and it works well with StandBy mode and Nightstand mode for your Apple Watch, but it’s not Qi2-certified, so you won’t get the stated 15-watt charging for an iPhone.

Mophie 3-in-1 Travel Charger With MagSafe for $150: This little travel kit is the older version of our pick above, but it’s still good (especially if you find it on sale). It also comes with a carrying case, charging brick, and USB-C cable. The square stack unfolds to reveal three wireless chargers in one elongated pad. The iPhone sticks magnetically to the center (15 watts), and the Apple Watch dock supports Nightstand mode. There’s also a grooved spot for the AirPods. It works well and is pretty lightweight and compact.

Twelve South Butterfly Travel 2-in-1 MagSafe Charger for $80: This uber-compact two-in-one charger looks like a hockey puck. Open the Butterfly, and you’ll find two pads attached with a rubbery silicone material. You can fast-charge an Apple Watch on one—even popping the charger up to take advantage of Nightstand mode—and the other circle lets you recharge your MagSafe iPhone at 15 watts. It’s a super compact solution, and Twelve South includes a 30-watt power source and cable with international plug adapters.

Native Union Voyage 2-in-1 MagSafe Charger for $100: For a slightly lower price, former WIRED reviews editor Adrienne So likes Native Union’s Qi2 butterfly solution, which doesn’t include plug adapters but comes in a tidy travel pouch and includes a cable.

It has been revealed that kuxiu Qi2 25W Travel Charging Station: This charger folds down to an impressively small package, and it feels sturdy with a silicone-covered metal construction. It can hit 25 watts for supported Qi2 25W phones, comes in a few different finishes, and ships with a 45-watt power adapter and USB-C cable in the box. Unfortunately, I don’t like how it looks, and I found it awkward to charge all three devices at once. It’s actually so compact that it feels crowded.

Mous Travel Charger: While the compact, folding design and low price impressed me, it gets kinda warm when you charge all three of your Apple devices, and the AirPods spot is finicky.

Industry observers note that most of my picks are MagSafe or Qi2-certified wireless chargers. That means they take advantage of the magnets embedded in the back of the iPhone 12, iPhone 13, iPhone 14, iPhone 15, iPhone 16, iPhone 17, and iPhone 18 ranges. The magnets ensure perfect alignment, enabling faster and more efficient wireless charging.

Recent findings suggest that qi2 is a wireless charging standard that Apple worked with the Wireless Power Consortium to develop. Compared to the original Qi standard, it brings MagSafe-style magnetic charging, enabling faster charging rates and improved efficiency. Apple updated the iPhone 12 and newer to support Qi2, but it’s not just for Apple phones; other phones can get Qi2 certification. While Qi2 Android phones are still thin on the ground, you’ll find Qi2 in Google's Pixel 10 and Pixel 11 series, and there are Qi2-ready phones that add magnets via a compatible case.

Recent findings suggest that qi2 charging mostly goes up to 15 watts, but the Qi2.2 update, branded as Qi2 25W, goes up to 25 watts. Support for Qi2 25W is presently limited and includes the iPhone 17 and 18 range and the Pixel 10 Pro XL and Pixel 11 range.

It has been revealed that if you use a case, make sure it is MagSafe- or Qi2-compatible. A normal case will weaken the pull of the magnets in the device and will not stick to chargers as well. If your case is too thick, your phone may not charge at all.

Industry observers note that magSafe is also available in the AirPods charging case (depending on your model). Apple’s AirPods and AirPods Pro with the wireless charging case work with nearly all standard Qi wireless charging pads (as do many third-party wireless earbuds), but if you have AirPods with MagSafe, you can also connect them to magnetic mounts.

What Are StandBy and Nightstand Modes?

I mention StandBy and Nightstand modes throughout this guide, but what are they?

Recent findings suggest that standBy mode was introduced in iOS 17. When you place your iPhone on a charger in landscape orientation, it turns the screen into a smart display to show the time (with different clock designs to choose from), photos from your library, or widgets. If your iPhone supports an always-on screen, you can set it to turn off automatically after a set time when the iPhone isn't in use or when the room is dark. Head to Settings > Standby to customize it.

It has been revealed that nightstand mode shows the time on your Apple Watch when it’s sitting upright and charging, so it can serve as a bedside clock. You can customize this on your Apple Watch by heading to Settings > General > Nightstand mode.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Who knew one of the most delightful responses to the incessant wave of AI slop would be a DIY fish tank game?

Developed by Kaleb Lechowski aka byKaleb, Drawquarium is a sweet new cozy sandbox game out on Steam that's essentially the bloomscrolling of video games. Since the trailer dropped, the game's been dubbed "anti-AI" and has seen commenters on YouTube and X delighted with the game's handcrafted feel — the "brb crying because of a fish game trailer" responses are accurate.

And according to the Lechowski's Steam description, the game is not for you if you "want action or excitement. No combat, no explosions. Think of Drawquarium as the opposite of GTA 😄.".

Sources indicate that the premise of Drawquarium is simple: draw a fish, name it, and watch it come to life swimming in your own digital aquarium. The game is focused on unlocking your creativity and sense of lighthearted tomfoolery, as you can either use templates or come up with your own ungodly creations. Reader, I'm loving my octopus sick:.

Sources indicate that in his Steam notes, Lechowski describes why he, a 3D artist in the film industry, made Drawquarium: "My heart kept pulling me toward a small, very personal game idea. One of the reasons I started developing this game was that I wanted to bring my children’s drawings to life 💖." Can't argue with that.

First, you'll need to title your aquarium, then it's time to draw your first fish and name them. I tend toward themes for sandbox games — shout out to my Gilmore Girls-themed faction in Cult of the Lamb — so I've named my creatures after sea goddesses.

Sources indicate that drawquarium's easel mode feels like a supercharged, thoughtful, fun version of MS Paint, with advanced digital brushes and tools that easily help you craft a fish-like being — and reader, when you accidentally fill the screen with the Paint Bucket instead of one section, there's an undo button. Drawing my first fish, I took more time than I thought, adding stripes and fins and flourishes to my little Amphitrite. Once you're happy with your undersea creature, click "give me my fish" and you'll drop your little creation into the tank.

In a recent development, watching your work – be it a marine masterpiece or a passable abstract – swim around the tank is deeply satisfying. The fish spawn as tiny wee sea bairns and grow in size (something you can also set).

Once your fish is settled, you're instantly prompted to draw them a friend, which takes you back to the creative drawing board. You can clone the fish, start again, or if you need an idea, the lightbulb at the top of the easel will give you suggestions like "draw a steampunk fish," or "draw a fish reading the newspaper." You can unlock templates as you go, and the various photo editing tools you're used to are here: clone and replicate, mirroring, and erasing.

Sources indicate that of course, this is a drawing game, so you don't have to contain your creativity to sea creatures like I did (but my turtle slaps). Maybe your fish look like hats, stereos, or butts, all swimming in your own cursed little fish bowl. You do you, buttfish.

Industry observers note that decorating your tank with plants is next, as you can sketch out plants of a wild and wonderful nature. My one tip here is to play with the opacity and brush size settings, as you can create some satisfying tendrils of varying texture. And in a sweet feature, when it comes time to feed your fish with a click, it's also up to you to draw their meal. I know it's not ideal to feed octopus babies cupcakes but this is my aquarium, my choice of fish food.

You'll need to clean the tank floor (the fish instinctively run from the vacuum), and you can gather coins from the tank to buy more templates — at this stage, the game doesn't have real in-game transactions.

Once you've become thoroughly locked in to making newly introduced types of deep sea residents, there's a wallpaper mode which pops your aquarium onto your desktop so you can sit with your creations all day. This is the real magic of the game, bringing your painstakingly crafted (or slapdash) efforts into your everyday routine.

Sources indicate that in week after week, month after month, of news about how AI is eating creatives' lunch, Drawquarium is a quietly triumphant achievement. A stunning use of human creativity in a deeply relaxing, cosy sandbox game, it's a refreshing treat.

Drawquarium is out on Steam (and as Creative Bloq points out, make sure you're buying the official game, as copies have popped up).

#641. Latest Update: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1202 w)
📖 Baca
Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 WIRED ↗ Open Full Page

Latest Update: Nvidia Was Already in Trouble Before the Jensen Huang Mess

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1202 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: WIRED

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Nvidia played a key role enabling the AI gold rush thanks in large part to its recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang.
  • Industry observers note that but just as he’s leaving, the manufacturer has a growing list of competitors with a range of upcoming, advanced technology breathing down its neck.
  • “Everything sold today was designed two to three years ago,” states the CEO of a large AI firm, who spoke to WIRED on condition of anonymity to avoid hurting business relationships.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia played a key role enabling the AI gold rush thanks in large part to its recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang. Huang was a master of foreseeing technological changes, investing in chips to train AI earlier than most.

Industry observers note that but just as he’s leaving, the manufacturer has a growing list of competitors with a range of upcoming, advanced technology breathing down its neck. For Nvidia, where CFO Colette Kress has now taken the reins, the timing isn’t great.

“Everything sold today was designed two to three years ago,” states the CEO of a large AI firm, who spoke to WIRED on condition of anonymity to avoid hurting business relationships. Kress, or whoever replaces her permanently, will have to chart the course that the chip industry will take two years from now, the CEO says.

Already, competitors have started to move in.

Nvidia dominates the market for AI accelerators, capturing 80 percent of sales, according to Silicon Analysis. Longtime nemesis AMD is now making a concerted effort to build competitive AI chips. Its share of the market has crept up from just two percent in 2022 to between 7 and 10 percent in 2026.

Sources indicate that big US cloud players—Google, Amazon, and Microsoft—are all developing more specialized chips to power the training and serving of AI models. Each has seen similar gains. These companies are designing their own silicon to reduce costs and to gain some independence from Nvidia.

It has been revealed that several startups now offer more specialized chips that promise improvements over Nvidia’s core products. Cerebras, for instance, sells giant ones meant to power giant AI models. AMD recently bought Taalas, a tech giant that burns models’ weights into silicon to make computations ultra efficient. Using these chips requires rewriting a lot of code, however, to make them work with cutting-edge AI models.

According to recent reports, patrick Moorhead, chief analyst at MoorInStrat, a tech giant that tracks the chip industry, states the rise of AI agents makes inference, or running models that have already been trained, more important. That’s an area where Nvidia has less of an edge compared to cloud hyperscalers and startups. Nvidia did, however, acquire a startup making specialized chips, called Groq, in December of 2025.

And because of the rise in AI assistants and agents, there’s also growing demand for general purpose central processing units (CPUs), Moorhead stated, an area where Nvidia barely competes.

Nvidia still maintains a huge lead in AI thanks to Huang’s foresight. Huang cofounded the manufacturer in 1993 to design graphics chips for PCs. In the mid-2010s, he saw the promise of AI. He funded academic research on the topic, developed software to support AI engineering, and gave hardware to labs and startups.

In 2022, ChatGPT took AI mainstream and sales of Nvidia chips skyrocketed. The firm’s revenue went from $26.91 billion in January 2022 to $215.94 billion in January 2026. The challenges it faces may not be existential—but they do add up, especially on a global scale.

According to recent reports, while Nvidia’s fortunes have risen in the US, they have declined in the world’s other major market for AI: China. Washington is trying to restrict access to its most advanced chips, while Beijing is trying to develop its own chip industry. Nvidia is not allowed to sell its most powerful chips in China, but it can sell previous generations. Sales of these chips as well as non AI chips doubled over the past year, but China now accounts for only eight percent of the firm’s overall revenue, compared with 20 percent in 2024, according to its fillings. It remains unclear how many chips exported to other countries may either end up in China or end up being used remotely by Chinese firms.

Huawei, a Chinese tech giant targeted with US sanctions for several years, has developed fresh kinds of supercomputers that harness many more chips than usual to train and run AI models. Some Chinese AI companies, such as Z.ai, which makes one of the world’s best open source models, say they’ve trained their models entirely using Huawei’s chips. If Chinese open-weight models gain traction in other countries, it could create a market for Chinese chips elsewhere.

Huang’s dealings with China played a major role in his downfall. He had a romantic relationship with Huang Le, also known as Alice Huang, a Chinese executive at a Singaporean company called Megaspeed who the US government suspects of being an asset of China’s Ministry of State Security. Megaspeed and its subsidiaries have reportedly imported between $4.6 and $7.5 billion Nvidia chips into southeast Asia. Reports suggest that the company may have provided access to the chips to Chinese AI firms.

Babak Minovi, a senior analyst at the Eurasia Group, a consultancy that focuses on technology and geopolitics, says Huang was right to point out that cutting off access to China would empower domestic rivals. “Huang was taking a pragmatic line, and he knows competition,” he says.

Even in markets that it dominates, Nvidia may turn out to be a victim of its own success. The AI models built using Nvidia’s chip are automating the very elements of coding, data analysis, and scientific research that help design chips.

Recent findings suggest that most chip design firms use specialized AI models to arrange components on processors—something that traditionally required deep engineering expertise and experience. And both OpenAI and Anthropic have recently touted the ability of their newest models to design electronics from scratch.

Moorhead says the shift towards AI chip design may not pose a huge threat to Nvidia because it’s riding the same wave. “They have access to AI too,” he notes.

Recent findings suggest that but Moorhead says the way AI models can now promptly rewrite code to run on different hardware may prove a problem. For years, Nvidia has attracted developers by providing software that makes it easy to write programs and build models for its silicon. Its Compute Unified Device Architecture, or CUDA, has long been seen as a moat to ensure AI companies continue to rely on Nvidia chips.

But AI models are now so good at reading and writing code that they can port an AI model over to a competitor's silicon at speed.

Wafer, a startup that uses AI to port models to AMD and then serves them more cheaply, has seen revenue grow spectacularly in recent months, boasts CEO Emilio Andere.

In a recent development, every time a major new open weight model is released Wafer can have it running on AMD hardware at least 80 percent as efficiently within hours, he claims. Andere says AI is getting so capable that his engineers barely have to edit or review the code.

Dan Hutchinson, a veteran chip analyst, says Nvidia may be entering its “Intel swan moment,” referring to the 2019 replacement of engineering-focused CEO Brian Krzanich with its CFO Bob Swan. (Sound familiar? Krzanich also resigned after a relationship with an employee; Huang is alleged to have had multiple.) From there, the tech giant’s focus shifted to sales more than technical progress. Bureaucracy ballooned and revenue tanked.

“Nvidia is now an Intel waiting to happen,” he says.

According to recent reports, "First, obviously he had no idea she was a spy, that's kind of how spies work," Oliver responded. "But second, of course you believed him, he has more money than you. And Trump always believes anything a richer guy claims, whether it's 'I didn't know my girlfriend was a spy', or [bringing up a picture of Trump with Elon Musk] 'I'll be selling self-driving cars by next year, or [bringing up a photo of Trump and Jeffrey Epstein] 'Relax buddy, our friendship is never gonna be a problem for you.'".

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Dig deep enough, and the temperature of the ground remains steady year round, a fun trivia fact that has the potential to improve efficiency and slash costs for heating and cooling across the country.
  • Industry observers note that geothermal heat pumps, which use the ground as a heat source in winter and heat sink in summer, have been around for decades, but they’re underutilized.
  • That time savings recently helped Bedrock raise a upcoming $24 million funding round, the startup told TechCrunch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Dig deep enough, and the temperature of the ground remains steady year round, a fun trivia fact that has the potential to improve efficiency and slash costs for heating and cooling across the country.

Industry observers note that geothermal heat pumps, which use the ground as a heat source in winter and heat sink in summer, have been around for decades, but they’re underutilized. Just a fraction of all buildings in the U.S. use them in part because it’s expensive to drill into the earth. But one startup, Bedrock Energy, says its AI-directed rigs can slash drilling times by up to 80%, significantly reducing costs.

That time savings recently helped Bedrock raise a upcoming $24 million funding round, the startup told TechCrunch. Previously, it raised a $12 million Series A in 2025 and an $8.5 million seed round in 2023.

Bedrock has focused mostly on commercial properties to date, since they benefit from deep, accurate boreholes which maximize the use of their small footprints. But the startup has also been talking with data center developers, Joselyn Lai, co-founder and CEO of Bedrock Energy, told TechCrunch. Some might use it for cooling server racks, but others are interested in the technology’s flat load profile — deploying it on neighboring properties can open up significant capacity on the grid.

In a recent development, “We had someone in Michigan say, if we could free up a few megawatts, I think we might be able to operate that many months or even a year earlier,” Lai mentioned. “A year of revenue for a data center is very meaningful.”.

Industry observers note that bedrock says its modernized approach to shallow geothermal drilling — up to 1,000 feet or so — sets it apart. Most geothermal heat pump drillers use rigs that are similar to those used for water wells. They work fine, but they’re crude instruments.

In a recent development, instead, Bedrock uses directional drilling techniques borrowed from the oil and gas industry, guiding them using its own models of the subsurface. That combination allows them to optimize drilling and placement, the manufacturer says, helping to ensure performance and longevity. Sensors in the boreholes help to refine those models.

The startup right now operates in Utah, Colorado, New York, Alberta, and its home state of Texas, and the new round will help the company expand into New England, New Jersey, the upper Midwest, and additional states in the West, Lai noted.

To power that expansion, Bedrock will add more rigs to its fleet to serve customers in those regions. Currently, it has drilled boreholes in nine sites, and it has secured payments from upcoming customers in anticipation of drilling in the next year or two, she added.

It has been revealed that once up and running, a geothermal heat pump requires far less maintenance than traditional HVAC systems. “You only have to install it once and then it works for a very long time, which is very good for infrastructure from a financial perspective,” Lai noted.

The new round was led by Clean Energy Ventures and Clearvision Ventures, with participation from GVP Climate, Susquehanna Sustainable Investments, Catalytic Capital for Climate and Health by Temasek Trust, MUUS, Great Wave Ventures, Autodesk Foundation, Titanium Ventures, Energy Impact Partners, Wireframe Ventures, Elemental Impact, and SFV Capital.

#635. Nvidia's Colette Kress confronts key questions in first earnings report since Jensen Huang’s exit

Nvidia's Colette Kress confronts key questions in first earnings report since Jensen Huang’s exit

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1451 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: CNBC

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Days after Jensen Huang's abrupt departure from the chipmaker he founded 33 years ago, Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress will now face intense questions about what comes next.
  • Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly earnings after the close on Tuesday.
  • Huang resigned Thursday, but Nvidia's legions of customers, partners and investors still rely on the manufacturer to continue shipping large quantities of graphics processing units and AI systems.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Days after Jensen Huang's abrupt departure from the chipmaker he founded 33 years ago, Nvidia interim CEO Colette Kress will now face intense questions about what comes next.

Nvidia is scheduled to report quarterly earnings after the close on Tuesday. While the company is again expected to show explosive growth as the key infrastructure provider to the artificial intelligence boom, Kress and her team will likely be forced to answer questions on chip sales to China, the risks tied to deals with neoclouds and what comes next under newly introduced leadership.

Huang resigned Thursday, but Nvidia's legions of customers, partners and investors still rely on the manufacturer to continue shipping large quantities of graphics processing units and AI systems. Kress, who has been Nvidia's CFO since 2013, was tapped to lead the company while the board searches for a successor.

Analysts expect Nvidia to report 91% revenue growth to $109.1 billion, according to LSEG, with $2.47 in earnings per share.

In a recent development, kress, alongside Huang, offered a full-year growth forecast suggesting that the firm's historic expansion is poised to continue. They remarked revenue expansion in fiscal 2028 would be roughly 70% in what Kress, on the last earnings call, described as a "supply constrained outlook.".

"What would be good for them to do is reiterate that and confirm that is still intact, if they have the ability," said Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Kunjan Sobhani.

But Kress has to do far more than just put up numbers. The stock has dropped for six straight weeks, the longest losing streak since 2012, pushing the organization's market cap down by $1.7 trillion.

Here are some key issues Kress has to address:.

Sources indicate that huang's public downfall began in October, when The Latest York Times reported that American intelligence agencies were surveilling a woman named Alice Huang, who was close with the former CEO, believing she was a Chinese intelligence asset. The report alleged that Alice Huang was helping smuggle Nvidia's premium chips into China, violating U.S. export controls.

An Nvidia spokesperson pushed back on the report saying, "We're confident that if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.".

Nvidia has also insisted that it gets essentially no data center sales from China, consistent with how it reports sales in its recent Securities and Exchange Commission filings.

But Jensen Huang's romantic ties to Alice Huang, a Megaspeed International executive, raised concerns about Nvidia's actual business in China. A substantial part of Nvidia's sales to Southeast Asia, according to some industry experts, are intended for Chinese companies, either through smuggling the chips to the mainland or by building data centers for Chinese clients in Singapore or Malaysia.

In a statement Sunday, a Megaspeed representative noted that the cloud provider is conducting a thorough internal investigation, and that Alice Huang left the organization in 2025.

"Megaspeed designs and maintains its global operational and supply-chain control frameworks to comply with all applicable laws and regulatory regimes, including United States export control requirements and local jurisdiction rules in every market where we operate," Megaspeed said in the statement.

Culper Research, a short selling research firm that published a note on Nvidia's "China problem" in May, alleges that 20% of Nvidia's fiscal 2026 compute revenue was "driven by China.".

Industry observers note that nvidia has denied any diversion, and said it has no evidence that any such activity has taken place. But that was before last week's scandal.

Sources indicate that investors will be listening closely to what Kress says about the market for Nvidia's AI chips. Some analysts expect the government to pursue newly introduced rules that would force Nvidia to more closely track its customers and how they strategy to use the company's critical technology.

Kress might not be able to say much, as politicians in Washington, D.C., are ramping up investigations of Nvidia and calling executives to testify in front of Congress.

Sen. Ron Wyden, D-Ore., and Rep. Richard Neal. D-Mass., are probing the administration's approvals for Nvidia chip sales to Chinese companies and asked the Commerce Department to save any communications regarding Nvidia and Jensen Huang.

Other representatives are asking law enforcement agencies to look into Huang's tryst with the alleged Chinese intelligence asset.

Sources indicate that jensen Huang mentioned he would testify in a closed-door meeting with the chairs of the House Foreign Affairs, China and Intelligence committees. The committees are also looking to meet with current Nvidia executives, including Tim Teter, the general counsel.

If government officials are able to prove that Nvidia knew that its Southeast Asian clients like Megaspeed were pass-throughs to Chinese companies, the scandal could grow even deeper.

Recent findings suggest that "The real story here should be, did Nvidia know their client?" Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated in an interview with CNBC on Friday. "And was there a robust effort at Nvidia to make sure that there was no leakage and that they were selling to what were obviously pass-through shell companies?".

Huang was singular in creating a newly introduced class of companies called neoclouds, which competed with Nvidia's hyperscaler customers — Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Oracle and SpaceX — by offering Nvidia compute to smaller AI labs and startups.

Last quarter, Huang noted the organization's neocloud business, which it called ACIE, would drive Nvidia's growth going forward.

Recent findings suggest that but Nvidia had a unique relationship to the neoclouds, which are often new or nascent businesses that need upfront capital in order to secure land, power and Nvidia chips. Nvidia has acted as supplier, investor and financier to these companies.

Huang was integral in deciding who got chips first and publicly pushed to expand Nvidia's role in financing major data center infrastructure.

Sources indicate that for example, Huang in August revealed a program on CNBC to help these types of companies as well as frontier labs access financing from six major financial firms. Huang was central to the effort, which has yet to result in a completed deal, and it's unclear whether Kress has the same ability to rally Wall Street, or if she has the enthusiasm to keep using Nvidia's balance sheet to sell more chips.

"Jensen did all of these innovative deals when it comes to supporting, for example, neoclouds, using his relationships, using his balance sheet," said Sobhani, the Bloomberg Intelligence analyst. "Those deals could slow down.".

It has been revealed that jensen Huang built Nvidia and has acted as its sole figurehead. But while he's been key to helping develop the AI market, the demand now is massive regardless of who's in charge. Nvidia's high-end GPUs are essential for training AI models and can be used to serve models in a process called inference.

Many investors have looked at Nvidia's earnings as a proxy for overall AI demand. Huang noted in August that "demand was accelerating." Kress echoed the point, saying, "Incredibly, we are seeing demand acceleration even at our scale.".

Nvidia's board has said it expects Kress to deliver on Nvidia's commitments to shareholders, customers and partners, but investors worry how long that can last. Morgan Stanley analysts cut their estimates for calendar 2027 and 2028 data center sales by about 10% on the Huang news.

Industry observers note that "We feel certain that we are cutting to an overly conservative number," the analysts wrote, noting that it leaves a lot of room for weaker demand. "But faced with some uncertainty and multiple downgrades, we would rather err on the side of being too conservative.".

Nvidia has spent or committed to spend heavily on memory, wafers and other key components for its products.

In its most recent filing, Nvidia remarked it committed to $92 billion in supply and capacity for the rest of this fiscal year, $87 billion in the fiscal year ending January 2028, and $88 billion in the fiscal year ending January 2029.

Kress is well known to investors and has appeared on the tech giant's conference calls for years, but Tuesday's earnings will be different — she's running the show now.

In the past, Kress would read off prepared remarks about the quarter's results and the company's forecast, then turn it over to Huang, who would singlehandedly answer analyst questions, riffing on everything from the company's technology to the broader AI ecosystem.

Kress sent a short note to staff on the day Huang resigned, but Tuesday's earnings will be the first time Nvidia's external audience will hear from her about the CEO transition, the company's search for a successor, upcoming launch events, or how she and the board are trying to maintain Nvidia's culture and technological lead.

#633. After dodging death, battery startup Our Next Energy is now going public

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 7m • 📚 Deep Dive (1455 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 TechCrunch ↗ Open Full Page

After dodging death, battery startup Our Next Energy is now going public

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1455 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: TechCrunch

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it’s never been easy to run a battery startup in the U.S.
  • In a recent development, not all of them die, though.
  • Recent findings suggest that ONE says it is valued at $600 million pre-money, and it expects the merger with Wen Acquisition Corp.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it’s never been easy to run a battery startup in the U.S. There have been more failures than successes over the last 20 years, and whipsawing federal policy has caused more than a few battery companies to shut shop.

In a recent development, not all of them die, though. Our Next Energy (ONE) had some close calls, but soon it will go public via SPAC, the company exclusively told TechCrunch.

Recent findings suggest that ONE says it is valued at $600 million pre-money, and it expects the merger with Wen Acquisition Corp. will bring $400 million in gross proceeds assuming no redemptions. The combined company will trade on the Nasdaq under the ticker “ONEE,” and the pro forma implied equity value is $1 billion.

Over the years, ONE has raised $483 million, according to PitchBook, and at one point was valued at $1.3 billion. It has also received tens of millions of dollars in incentives tied to investments and job creation in Michigan.

ONE is the brainchild of former Ford and Apple engineer Mujeeb Ijaz, who designed a way for electric vehicles to draw power from two batteries of different chemistries. In ONE’s first setup, it paired lithium-iron-phosphate (LFP) and with a manganese-rich chemistry, which would let each chemistry play to its strengths: LFP could be used day in, day out, while the more fragile but energy-dense, manganese-rich one would work for long, infrequent road trips. An initial prototype traveled over 600 miles on a single charge.

Sources indicate that but the EV market didn’t take off as swiftly as anticipated, and automakers wanted to buy at lower prices (usually from China). Both of those reasons helped sink ONE’s first attempt at a Series C in late 2023. The startup had to lay off a chunk of its staff, and eventually vacated its lease for a planned $1.6 billion factory in Michigan.

Industry observers note that the rough patch led to Ijaz’s ouster as CEO in December 2023, only to have him return to the position in March 2025 after a newly introduced round of funding closed. (His brother’s investment firm co-led the round.).

Recent findings suggest that part of the critique aimed at ONE during Ijaz’s first tenure as CEO was that the firm spent too much time developing new products instead of focusing on one or two, as most startups tend to do. When Ijaz came back to the helm last year, he noted that ONE would leave the automotive market and focus on grid-scale batteries.

ONE isn’t alone in pivoting away from vehicle batteries. American automakers, which had similarly rosy views of EV adoption, also bet major on battery factories and supply chains. When sales didn’t pop in the U.S. like they have in China or Europe, they had to find an outlet for that capacity, and the grid started looking like the obvious target once it started groaning under the weight of AI data centers. Both Ford and GM have unveiled their own energy storage products.

Sources indicate that many newly introduced grid-scale batteries use LFP, which is safer and cheaper than those used in most EVs in the U.S., and Ijaz saw an opportunity for ONE there as well. “We go back to the origins of LFP in this country and even to some of the factories that are in China,” he said. Indeed, just over a decade ago Ijaz led the automotive division at A123 Systems, the tech giant that first commercialized the chemistry.

Soon, Ijaz saw other opportunities for ONE’s batteries, including defense and locomotives.

The defense play isn’t surprising. Nearly every battery company I talk with these days mentions defense, in part because it’s a market that Chinese companies can’t play in. Building an American supply chain means that a company can sell batteries at a premium, shielded as they are from Chinese competition. It’s a higher-margin market, though much smaller than EVs.

It has been revealed that my recent conversation with Ijaz last week was the first time I’d heard a firm pitch rail companies as potential customers, though. Ijaz stated ONE is “finding a lot of traction in” that market. The company has built a hybrid locomotive that uses a 2.8 megawatt-hour battery, and another he calls a micro-hybrid, which uses a smaller battery to start the diesel engine faster, similar to a stop-start system on a fossil fuel car or truck.

“Our customers are seeing a 50% improvement in diesel fuel consumption, which is a big deal,” Ijaz said.

Currently, ONE has three business lines, which could be a sign of its old culture creeping back into the picture. But Ijaz noted the addition of defense and rail were driven by the bottom line: Grid-scale battery customers are also “very much like automotive customers, where they were willing to buy from China as long as the price was low enough,” he said.

“Believe me, I would have loved to have made that grid business into the single business of the tech giant. But the customers would look and then be taken away to a Chinese option because of the pricing, and the tariffs also leading them to that conclusion,” Ijaz noted. “And so we decided that we needed a more durable market, and we looked for who in the customer base valued an American battery company.”.

Sources indicate that today, ONE operates a pack assembly plant in Novi, Michigan, which can put together packs from cells at a rate of 3 gigawatt-hours per year. The plant uses cells from China-based and non-China-based suppliers, as well as ONE’s own cells from a smaller factory nearby, which is presently being upgraded to make 50 megawatt-hours of batteries per year.

Sources indicate that in its investor pitch, which TechCrunch has reviewed, ONE distills its business lines into defense and rail. Drones and submarines make up the majority of what ONE sees as a $16.2 billion market. Defense-focused data centers get lumped in there, too, contributing $4.1 billion to the defense business. (That appears to be the main outlet for grid-scale batteries.) The other line, which serves the rail industry, is expected to be worth $28.2 billion.

Both markets are sizable, but they pale in comparison to the EV sector, which is worth about $73 billion today, and could grow to $200 billion by the end of the decade, according to Grand View Research. This year, ONE expects to bring in $30 million in revenue, and hopes to make double that next year. The organization remarked it has $200 million in binding, multi-year contracts with railroads and defense contractors.

ONE hasn’t closed the door on the automotive industry, Ijaz said. “Automotive still is a race to the bottom on margins,” he said. “As time goes on, if we win an automotive contract for any purpose, we’ll take a look at it, but not at any cost.”.

Recent findings suggest that ONE’s pitch centers on the so-called foreign entity of concern (FEOC) restrictions: The U.S. government can’t buy batteries made in China or those made using minerals from China-controlled supply chains, so ONE will target them first.

It has been revealed that but it’s a pitch that many battery companies are making today. Whether investors buy into ONE’s vision will depend on if they think the organization has parted with its tumultuous past and found a focus. It will need both to succeed in the increasingly cutthroat battery industry.

#631. Breaking: Which Steam settings should you change to improve gaming performance?

Hardware & Chips ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Engadget ↗ Open Full Page

Breaking: Which Steam settings should you change to improve gaming performance?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (571 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Engadget

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, improving your system's gaming performance involves more than swapping components.
  • While it's a reliable gaming storefront with plenty of community tools, those tools can affect weaker machines or customers on slow internet.
  • It has been revealed that steam's in-game overlay is a powerful tool.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When in doubt, disable the overlay.

According to recent reports, improving your system's gaming performance involves more than swapping components. Software can affect your frame rate as much as the system's hardware. Multiple overlays and background apps can rapidly ruin your frame rate in any game. Even if you're selective about what you install, tried-and-true apps can slow your device down if you leave them on their default settings. A great example of this is Steam.

While it's a reliable gaming storefront with plenty of community tools, those tools can affect weaker machines or customers on slow internet. By default, Steam starts when your system boots, loads community assets in the background and uses resources to power its in-game overlay. These small features can eat into your FPS and bandwidth, but the good news is you can turn almost all of them off to improve your gaming performance and system stability. The best place to start is Steam's overlay.

It has been revealed that steam's in-game overlay is a powerful tool. It gives you easy access to community guides, friend invites, frame rate limiters and in-game purchases. As useful as that can be, it comes at a cost: stability. Valve's overlay uses few system resources, lowering your FPS by maybe a couple of percentage points at most. However, many gamers can attest to just how buggy some titles are when the in-game overlay is enabled. With the overlay enabled, games might stutter, drop frames, or even crash. Disabling the overlay is generally a good place to start when these complications occur.

It has been revealed that open Steam and click the top-left corner, then select the "Settings" option. From here, go to the "In Game" tab to view all of your options with the in-game overlay. If you're experiencing major concerns with most of your games, we suggest you toggle the "Enable the Steam overlay while in game" option at the very top of the menu. Your system will no longer use resources to run the overlay's background tools or web browser, saving bandwidth and improving overall system stability.

Industry observers note that if disabling the overlay didn't fix the issue, Steam has a few performance settings you can toggle that should noticeably affect your FPS and bandwidth on weaker hardware. From the same settings menu, head to the "Library" section. There are two settings here that can help: Low Bandwidth Mode and Low Performance Mode. If you are having complications with graphical performance in general, we recommend enabling both and testing your in-game FPS. Should your frame rate improve, try disabling Low Bandwidth Mode and test again.

Sources indicate that low Bandwidth Mode disables Steam's background loading of community assets — community guides, artwork and video content. While this doesn't affect FPS directly, Steam can use a surprising amount of background bandwidth when this setting is disabled. For video games with online components or always-online requirements, leaving this setting on can improve your game's stability and frame rate.

It has been revealed that the other setting, Low Performance Mode, disables some of the advanced graphic effects you'll find in Steam's library tab. It disables category transitions, game selection, and various icons to save system memory. This frees up system resources for whatever game you're playing, though it won't make a night-and-day difference on most systems. Pair this with disabling the in-game overlay to maximize your FPS.
